chunks: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said:

Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in every night of the month of Ramadan there are those freed and released from the Fire, except one who breaks his fast upon an intoxicant. Then when its last night comes, He frees in it the like of what He freed in all of it.

key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month of sawm
key_terms.طُلَقَاءَ: those released, referring here to people released from the Fire
key_terms.عُتَقَاءَ: those set free, meaning persons emancipated from punishment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about being freed from the Fire during Ramadan and the ruling on breaking the fast with an intoxicant?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, frees people from the Fire on every night of the month of Ramadan. It warns that breaking the fast with an intoxicant deprives one of this grace, and it highlights the immense merit of the final night, in which as many are freed as in the whole month.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1838 - It is narrated by Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)), who said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, has freed individuals from the Fire every night of the Month of Ramadan, except for those who break their fast with an intoxicant. On the last night of the month, He frees as many as He freed throughout the entire month."
